advances: Lattice-complete product with (n=d), ordinary mixed (d)-volume, and an exact globally critical menu.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
The lattice census proved in 11ed3ca552482ee9 with $n=d$ gives $D\cap\mathbb Z^d=\{0,v_0,\ldots,v_d\}$. Thus all $d+2$ actual fibers equal $K$ and the mixed Hausdorff $d$-volume is $(d+2)V$. The functions $\ell_j$ sum to zero; $\ell_j(v_j)=d$, $\ell_j(v_i)=-1$ for $i\ne j$, and $\ell_j(0)=0$. Hence $H_j$ strictly captures the whole outer fiber at $v_j$, misses all other outer fibers strictly, and takes the canonical centroid cap of volume $\gamma_d V$ at zero. Its margin plus the other $d$ margins sums to zero identically because $\sum_j\lambda_j=1$, giving whole-space coverage and the upper bound $Q$.

For the lower bound at $(0,g)$, move any closed containing halfspace inward until it passes through $(0,g)$ and write its margin as $a\cdot z+u\cdot(x-g)$. On the middle fiber the full-mass specialization of 6769574fc1bd9f8d guarantees at least $\gamma_dV$ if $u\ne0$, and the whole middle fiber is captured if $u=0$. For the outer fibers, take one uniform point of $K$ and use its $d+1$ cyclic barycentric permutations $X_j$, one at $v_j$. Each permutation is an affine automorphism preserving uniform volume, and $\sum_j X_j=(d+1)g$ pointwise. Together with $\sum_j v_j=0$, this makes the sum of their margins zero. At least one pair $(v_j,X_j)$ is therefore captured in every sample. Taking expectations over the uniform marginals gives outer capture at least $V$, including pure integer normals and equality margins. Thus the original $H_j$ genuinely attain depth at $(0,g)$.

Each outer vertex is exposed. A large finite exposing slope isolates that fiber without changing a chosen through-source continuous trace there. Choosing the smaller of two opposite continuous traces gives depth at most $V/2<Q$ at each outer point. At a different middle point $x$, some $\lambda_j(x)>1/(d+1)$; moving the threshold of $H_j$ to $\lambda_j(x)$ in the margin $\lambda_j(\cdot)+\ell_j(z)$ still captures exactly the same whole outer fiber and misses the other outer fibers. The middle mass $(1-\lambda_j(x))^dV$ is now strictly smaller than $\gamma_dV$, so this proves uniqueness.

The gradients of the barycentric coordinates have rank $d$ and their sole linear relation is the sum-zero relation. The strict outer statuses imply there are no sections there. On the central section $\lambda_j=1/(d+1)$, the other $d$ barycentric coordinates form a simplex with sum $d/(d+1)$; their means are all $1/(d+1)$, so its centroid is $g$. At a proper threshold $s$, the negative derivative of $(1-s)^dV$ gives the coarea mass for $\nabla\lambda_j$, hence the stated value at $s=1/(d+1)$. The section meets the fiber boundary in a finite union of sets of dimension at most $d-2$. Thus the equal coarea weights use no supporting-face correction.
statement:
For each $d\ge2$, put $v_0=(-1,\ldots,-1)$, $v_i=e_i$ for $1\le i\le d$, and $D=\operatorname{conv}\{v_0,\ldots,v_d\}\subset\mathbb R^d$. Let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be any simplex of volume $V>0$, with barycentric coordinates $\lambda_0,\ldots,\lambda_d$ and centroid $g$. Set $C=D\times K$ with integer coordinates in $D$. Let $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$ and set $\ell_0(z)=-\sum_i z_i$, $\ell_i(z)=(d+1)z_i-\sum_j z_j$ for $i\ge1$. The $d+1$ closed ambient caps
$
H_j=\{(z,x):\lambda_j(x)-1/(d+1)+\ell_j(z)\ge0\}
$
cover all of ambient space and all have mass $Q=(1+\gamma_d)V$. The unique global deepest point on the actual lattice sample of $C$ is $(0,g)$, with normalized depth $(1+\gamma_d)/(d+2)$.

At that point the caps are a positive critical circuit. Their only nonempty cut sections among the integer fibers are proper on the middle fiber; the section centroids are $(0,g)$ and their coarea masses for the displayed continuous normals are all $d(d/(d+1))^{d-1}V$. In particular the normalized inverse-coarea response weights are all $1/(d+1)$.
title: Exact critical depth on a simplex with one interior lattice base
